title: How to use AVERAGE in Excel
description: Learn how to calculate averages in Excel with the AVERAGE function. See clear examples, avoid common mistakes, and practice hands-on.

args.name: number1
args.text: The first number, cell reference, or range to average.

args.name: number2
args.text: More numbers, references, or ranges to include in the average.

sections.heading: What AVERAGE does
sections.text: **AVERAGE** calculates the mean of a group of numbers. Give it individual numbers or a range such as `B2:B6`, and it returns their average. Text and completely empty cells in the range are ignored.

sections.heading: A small example
sections.text: Here are daily volunteer hours. The formula in the blank result cell calculates the average hours worked across the three days.

sections.heading: Average separate ranges
sections.text: You can include multiple ranges by separating them with commas: `=AVERAGE(B2:B4,D2:D4)`. Excel combines all the numbers and divides by the total count.

sections.heading: Common mistake: blank cells versus zeros
sections.text: Excel ignores empty cells, but it counts cells that contain `0`. If you enter `0` for a missed day, it pulls the average down. Leave the cell blank if you want Excel to skip it. Also note that a range with no numbers returns a `#DIV/0!` error.
